context_resolution.explanation: No confirmed book or reading boundary yet; Muse will call librarian_route during its own turn if the request appears to depend on a specific book.

observed.reply:
That awkwardness makes sense: “designer” names the work you already know how to do, while “manager” may still feel like a role you’re growing into. Naming it can feel less like stating a fact and more like claiming an identity before it feels fully settled.

You don’t have to pretend the transition is complete. You could try:

- “Hi, I’m [name]. I recently moved from design into a management role, and I’m enjoying learning the work from this side.”
- “I’m [name], the manager for this team. My background is in design, so I’m bringing that perspective into the role.”
- “I’m [name]. I lead this team now, after working as a designer, and I’m glad to be here.”

The most honest version may be one that holds both truths: you are a manager now, and you are still a designer by background and instinct. Which part feels hardest to say aloud—the word “manager,” the sense that you have to sound authoritative, or the feeling that “designer” is being left behind?

Muse repeats that question after Provenance requests revision; the second review also requests revision and the application releases a generic safe decline. No boundary judgment or grounding call runs.
scenes.interpretation: An offline probe of the actual configured Librarian reproduces equal routing confidence: Alice matches alice/pigeon, while Pinocchio matches pigeon/serpent. Generic story cues create a competing work despite the named Alice reference. This same route failure appears in the saved September 13 run; the new passage-assessment input is never reached. Most failed checks are consequences of this earlier routing failure.
scenes.grade_reliability: The missing quotation and wrong route are directly observed, so failure is credible. The many boundary, provenance, and citation failures are not independent defects. Provenance’s objection to application-owned catalog names may also need separate review; fixing passage assessment cannot resolve this earlier route.
scenes.next_step: Fix work identification so an unambiguous named-work reference outranks incidental shared story cues, preserving clarification when two works are actually named. Then verify boundary inference and quotation release through an authorised replay.
